payload.task_text:
You are an inventory manager responsible for monitoring product stock levels and coordinating restocking activities for an online store. Your goal is to analyze the current product inventory, forecast demand, generate reports, and ensure timely restock scheduling.

Start by reading the Inventory_Policy.pdf in your workspace, which describes the reorder thresholds and lead time expectations. Also review the warehouse_config.json file that contains warehouse capacity limits and supplier contact information.

Query the e-commerce platform to retrieve the complete product catalog. For each product, gather the product name, category, regular price, stock quantity, stock status, and total sales count. You will use this data to assess inventory health and compute reorder priorities.

Write a Python script called demand_forecast.py in your workspace and execute it using command-line tools. The script should compute a simple demand velocity metric for each product by dividing total sales by an assumed 180-day selling period to get daily sales rate. Then calculate days of supply by dividing current stock quantity by the daily sales rate (use 999 for products with zero sales rate). Determine a reorder point for each product as 14 times the daily sales rate (representing a 14-day lead time buffer). Flag products as Critical urgency if their current stock is at or below the reorder point and they are not out of stock, flag out-of-stock products as Out_of_Stock urgency, and flag all others as Normal.

Create an Excel workbook called Inventory_Lifecycle_Report.xlsx in your workspace with four sheets.

The first sheet should be named Product_Inventory and contain columns for product_name, category, price, stock_qty, stock_status, total_sales, and days_of_supply. Include one row for every product in the catalog, sorted by days_of_supply ascending so the most urgent items appear first.

The second sheet should be named Reorder_Alerts and contain columns for product_name, current_stock, reorder_point, and urgency. Include only the products that have Critical or Out_of_Stock urgency, sorted by urgency with Out_of_Stock items first.

The third sheet should be named Category_Summary and contain columns for category, product_count, avg_stock, and total_value. Total value should be the sum of price times stock quantity for each product in the category. Include one row per product category.

The fourth sheet should be named Restock_Schedule and contain columns for product_name, reorder_date, quantity, and supplier. For each Critical or Out_of_Stock product, set the reorder date to March 10, 2026. The quantity to order should be the reorder point minus current stock (minimum 1 unit). The supplier should be "Primary Supplier" for all items.

Publish the Category_Summary data to the shared spreadsheet system so the team can view real-time inventory status. Create a spreadsheet titled "Inventory Dashboard" with a sheet containing the category summary data.

Schedule a restock review meeting on the shared calendar for March 11, 2026 at 10:00 AM lasting one hour. The event summary should be "Inventory Restock Review Meeting" and the description should mention the number of critical items identified.

Send an email to purchasing@company.com with the subject "Critical Inventory Alert - Restock Required" summarizing the number of out-of-stock and critical products, along with the top three most urgent items that need immediate restocking.
Note: Use the America/New_York timezone for all calendar events in this task.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent freezes every source fact and computed metric into one canonical payload first, then dispatches exactly one wave of two parallel coder sub-agents (workbook writer and external-services writer). No plan agent is used: the frozen payload and the two writer contracts below are the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace, read Inventory_Policy.pdf and warehouse_config.json, and freeze their thresholds and supplier facts. Retrieve the complete WooCommerce catalog with woo_products_list(page=1,perPage=100), continuing only when pagination requires it, and retrieve complete categories. Require 82 unique live product IDs, preserve every category membership plus literal regular_price, stock_quantity, stock_status and total_sales, and use full_output_path if the response is oversized. Write and run demand_forecast.py: daily_sales=total_sales/180; days_supply=stock/daily_sales or 999 for zero-rate products; reorder_point=14*daily_sales; urgency Out_of_Stock first, then Critical when stock<=reorder_point, else Normal; order_qty=reorder_point-stock (minimum 1 unit) with reorder_date 2026-03-10 and supplier "Primary Supplier". Read the script and its output back, then freeze one canonical inventory_metrics.json in the workspace containing: the full 82-row inventory list sorted by days_of_supply ascending, the Reorder_Alerts rows (Critical and Out_of_Stock only, Out_of_Stock items first), the Category_Summary rows (category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value=regular_price*stock), the Restock_Schedule rows, and the top-three most urgent items with complete product names plus the out-of-stock and critical counts. This file is the single binding input for both sub-agents; after the freeze nobody re-reads the store, the PDF, the config, or the script.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming inventory_metrics.json verbatim with no recomputation and no source-system reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Inventory_Lifecycle_Report.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly four sheets: Product_Inventory with columns product_name, category, price, stock_qty, stock_status, total_sales, days_of_supply and all 82 rows sorted by days_of_supply ascending; Reorder_Alerts with columns product_name, current_stock, reorder_point, urgency and only Critical/Out_of_Stock rows, Out_of_Stock first; Category_Summary with columns category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value, one row per category; Restock_Schedule with columns product_name, reorder_date, quantity, supplier and the frozen March 10, 2026 rows. Write literal values only, read all four populated ranges back, and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): External-services writer — sole owner of the three external outputs. Fully paginate the exact-title search for cloud spreadsheet Inventory Dashboard, create/reuse at most once, block duplicate titles/tabs, own exactly one Category_Summary tab, batch-write the frozen category rows and read them back; search the exact Inventory Restock Review Meeting on 2026-03-11 10:00-11:00 America/New_York, create at most once with the frozen critical-item count in the description, and get_event; paginate Sent search/read candidates for purchasing@company.com and exact subject Critical Inventory Alert - Restock Required, send at most once with the frozen out-of-stock/critical counts and the top three complete item names, then read it back.

After Wave 1, verify both handoffs in one single pass (never per-branch iteration) against inventory_metrics.json: workbook cell-for-cell, dashboard rows, event identity and email contents. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 1.

You are the OFFICE-REPORT-BUILDER for an inventory task. Your single deliverable is an Excel workbook `Inventory_Lifecycle_Report.xlsx` in the workspace. You must NOT read any source system (WooCommerce, PDF, config), must NOT recompute any metric, and must NOT touch any file other than the payload you read (read-only) and the workbook you create.

SOURCE OF TRUTH (read this file only, with Python json.load, treat every value as final and verbatim):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-wc-excel-gsheet-gcal-email/workspace/inventory_metrics.json

Its structure:
- payload["product_inventory"]: 82 dicts with keys product_name, category, price, stock_qty, stock_status, total_sales, days_of_supply (already sorted by days_of_supply ascending — preserve order).
- payload["reorder_alerts"]: 29 dicts with keys product_name, current_stock, reorder_point, urgency (already sorted, Out_of_Stock first — preserve order).
- payload["category_summary"]: 8 dicts with keys category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value.
- payload["restock_schedule"]: 29 dicts with keys product_name, reorder_date, quantity, supplier.

DELIVERABLE: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-wc-excel-gsheet-gcal-email/workspace/Inventory_Lifecycle_Report.xlsx — create it EXACTLY ONCE with EXACTLY four worksheets, in this order, using the mcp__excel__ tools:

1. Sheet "Product_Inventory": header row [product_name, category, price, stock_qty, stock_status, total_sales, days_of_supply] then all 82 data rows from payload["product_inventory"] in the given order. Write literal values only (NO formulas). price/days_of_supply as numbers, stock_qty/total_sales as integers.
2. Sheet "Reorder_Alerts": header row [product_name, current_stock, reorder_point, urgency] then all 29 rows from payload["reorder_alerts"] in the given order.
3. Sheet "Category_Summary": header row [category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value] then all 8 rows from payload["category_summary"] in the given order.
4. Sheet "Restock_Schedule": header row [product_name, reorder_date, quantity, supplier] then all 29 rows from payload["restock_schedule"] in the given order.

Workflow with mcp__excel__ tools (all operations target the single filepath above):
- create_workbook(filepath). Then call get_workbook_metadata to see the default sheet(s). Rename the default sheet to "Product_Inventory" (rename_worksheet) so it becomes sheet 1; otherwise create Product_Inventory as the first sheet and delete the default. Then create_worksheet for "Reorder_Alerts", "Category_Summary", "Restock_Schedule" so the final sheet order is exactly: Product_Inventory, Reorder_Alerts, Category_Summary, Restock_Schedule. Delete any leftover default sheets. Do not create extra sheets.
- Use write_data_to_excel(filepath, sheet_name, data=[header]+rows, start_cell="A1") for each sheet (data must be a list of lists; numbers as Python int/float, dates as the string "2026-03-10", supplier as the string).
- Do NOT apply formulas, formatting is optional (bold headers allowed but not required).

MANDATORY VERIFICATION (read back everything you wrote):
- get_workbook_metadata(filepath) → confirm exactly the 4 sheets in the required order.
- For each sheet, read_data_from_excel(filepath, sheet_name, start_cell="A1", end_cell=<last cell>) and confirm: row counts (82 data rows + header for Product_Inventory; 29+1 for Reorder_Alerts; 8+1 for Category_Summary; 29+1 for Restock_Schedule) and that EVERY cell value equals the corresponding payload value. Compare programmatically if possible (e.g., load with python json and cross-check the read-back). Report any mismatch explicitly.

RETURN (in your final message): absolute path of the workbook, final sheet order, row counts per sheet, and a per-sheet PASS/FAIL equality statement with any mismatches. Do not call claim_done.
Build Inventory_Lifecycle_Report.xlsx

You are the EXTERNAL-WORKFLOW-OPERATOR for an inventory task. You own exactly three external outputs: a Google Sheets dashboard, a Google Calendar event, and an email. You must NOT recompute any metric and must NOT read any source system. Every value comes verbatim from the frozen payload.

SOURCE OF TRUTH (read this file only, with Python json.load, treat every value as final):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-wc-excel-gsheet-gcal-email/workspace/inventory_metrics.json

Key values you will need:
- payload["category_summary"]: 8 rows, each {category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value} (order: Audio, Cameras, Electronics, Headphones, Home Appliances, Speakers, TV & Home Theater, Watches).
- payload["meta"]["critical_count"] = 24; payload["counts"]["out_of_stock"] = 5, payload["counts"]["critical"] = 24.
- payload["top_three_urgent"]: list of the 3 most urgent item names (use the FULL names verbatim).

A) GOOGLE SHEETS DASHBOARD (mcp__google_sheet__ tools):
1. Search for an existing spreadsheet whose TITLE is exactly "Inventory Dashboard": use search_spreadsheets(query="Inventory Dashboard", max_results=100) and also list_spreadsheets() to inspect the default folder. Filter candidates by title == "Inventory Dashboard".
   - If exactly one exists → REUSE it. If none exists → create_spreadsheet(title="Inventory Dashboard"). If multiple exist → reuse the first one; NEVER create a second spreadsheet with this title.
2. Ensure there is EXACTLY ONE tab holding the category summary data (prefer reusing the spreadsheet's default first sheet; if a tab named "Category_Summary" already exists, reuse it; otherwise rename the default sheet to "Category_Summary" or create_sheet(title="Category_Summary")). Do not create duplicate tabs with the same name.
3. Write to that single tab starting at A1 via update_cells/batch_update_cells: header row [category, product_count, avg_stock, total_value] followed by the 8 data rows from payload["category_summary"] in the given order (numbers as numbers).
4. Read the tab back (get_sheet_data) and verify every cell (header + 8 rows) equals the payload values. Report the spreadsheet_id, tab name, and PASS/FAIL equality.

B) GOOGLE CALENDAR EVENT (mcp__google_calendar__ tools), timezone America/New_York:
1. Search for an existing event "Inventory Restock Review Meeting" on 2026-03-11: list_events(timeMin="2026-03-11T00:00:00-05:00", timeMax="2026-03-11T23:59:59-05:00"). If an event with that exact summary already exists, reuse it (do not create a duplicate).
2. Otherwise create_event: summary="Inventory Restock Review Meeting", start={"dateTime":"2026-03-11T10:00:00","timeZone":"America/New_York"}, end={"dateTime":"2026-03-11T11:00:00","timeZone":"America/New_York"}, description must mention the number of critical items identified, e.g. "Inventory restock review for the 24 critical items identified in the inventory analysis." (use payload["meta"]["critical_count"]).
3. Verify with get_event(eventId) and report event id, summary, start, end, timezone, description.

C) EMAIL TO purchasing@company.com (mcp__emails__ tools):
1. Check whether the email already exists: search_emails(query="Critical Inventory Alert - Restock Required", folder="Sent") (and check INBOX too). If an email with that exact subject to purchasing@company.com already exists, do NOT send again — report its id instead.
2. Otherwise send via send_email: to="purchasing@company.com", subject="Critical Inventory Alert - Restock Required", body (plain text) must summarize: the number of out-of-stock products (5) and critical products (24) from payload["counts"], and the top three most urgent items needing immediate restock with their COMPLETE names from payload["top_three_urgent"] (list all three names verbatim). Example body structure: "Dear Purchasing Team,\n\nThis is a critical inventory alert. Currently 5 products are out of stock and 24 products are at or below reorder point (Critical). The top three most urgent items requiring immediate restock are:\n1. <name1>\n2. <name2>\n3. <name3>\n\nPlease prioritize restocking these items.\n\nBest regards,\nInventory Management"
3. Verify by searching Sent for the exact subject and reading the sent email (read_email) to confirm recipient, subject, and that the body contains the counts and the three item names. Report email id, to, subject, date.

CONSTRAINTS: create each external artifact AT MOST ONCE — never duplicates (no duplicate spreadsheet titles, no duplicate tabs, no duplicate calendar events, no duplicate emails). Use America/New_York for the calendar event. Do not modify anything else. Do not call claim_done. RETURN in your final message: spreadsheet id + tab name + equality result, event id + full event details, email id + details, and all verification results.
External services: sheets, calendar, email
